$description: Paper pillar — semantic layer. Each document family/sub-domain selects margins, rules, type, and color from paper/primitive.json. Seven families: legal-subscription-agreement, prospectus, agency-suite, financial-statement-yearend, financial-report-layout, pdf-binder, paper-legal (cross-cutting drafting-convention taxonomy — see paper-legal-conventions below for the non-DTCG qualitative rules it also carries).

legal-subscription-agreement.$description: Subscription-agreement family (accredited investor + Family & Friends variants — same recipe, differing schedule variants). Renamed 2026-07-23 from 'legal-agreement' — that name collided with project-documents' own templates/legal-agreement.css, an unrelated Shareholder/Constitutional-agreement family. See paper-legal recipe.json oq-1 (now closed) and this file's constitutional-agreement description below, updated in the same pass.

ordinal-marker.$description: Two-level hanging-indent ordinal system for nested sub-clauses. WeasyPrint 61.1 ignores both the HTML type= attribute and ::marker { content } trailing whitespace (confirmed via direct render test 2026-07-22) — this family uses a counter-reset + ::before + position:absolute technique instead, NOT the .cl1/.cl2/.cl3 span-based mechanism used by legal-agreement.css/commercial-agreement.css (36pt/18pt) or cim.css (22pt/18pt). This is a real, deliberate divergence between families, not drift — see 'Open questions' in the originating DESIGN-TOKEN-CHANGE draft.

third-level.$value: none — (A)/(B)/(C) sub-markers stay inline text within the nested item, per the source docx's own structure; not a real third list level

continuation-indent.$description: Shares the ordinal system's 20pt indent grid — used by .indent for plain indented paragraphs outside a list (e.g. continuation text that isn't itself a sub-clause).

schedule-instruction.$description: Centered italic gating line for schedule-specific eligibility notices (e.g. Schedule B-1/B-2's "Complete this schedule only if..." line). Existed inline in the original Client-A-specific documents; promoted to the canonical stylesheet alongside form-note (same commit, same additive-only status).

address-block.$description: Set-off, non-justified indented block for regulator contact addresses and similar multi-line inserts inside an otherwise-justified list item. Added 2026-07-22 (commit 572b987) after the source docx samples showed these as their own indented lines, not run-on prose.

schedule-footer-format.$description: Per-schedule page-footer numbering. Single-letter schedules (A/B/C) use the established no-hyphen form; multi-character schedule IDs (B1/B2, Friends & Family only) use a hyphenated form — added 2026-07-22 after confirming the unhyphenated form collided in rendered text with the parent schedule's own numbering (Schedule B's own page 11 and Schedule B1's page 1 both printed "- B11 -").

single-letter.$description: Backed by templates/subscription-form.css's own @page schedule-a/b/c rules — verified present in the canonical file.

multi-character.$description: PROVENANCE CORRECTION (caught by Fable coverage review, 2026-07-23): this rule does NOT currently exist in templates/subscription-form.css — it lives only inline in the Friends & Family HTML's own <style> block. Transcribed from the live HTML, not the canonical CSS mirror. The canonical file arguably should gain these rules — that's a project-documents-side CSS change, out of scope for this token draft.

financial-statement-yearend.$description: Statutory year-end financial statements (Notice to Reader / compilation register). Portrait, symmetric 1in margins, pure black-on-white.

financial-report-layout.$description: Proforma / projection dashboard register — landscape, wide multi-period tables. Explicitly a sibling of financial-statement-yearend, not the same register (different page geometry, density, and tone). Dashboard-theme values below; statement-theme values are PROVISIONAL pending the not-yet-implemented proforma engine work (BRIEF-client-a-proforma-engine-recapitalization.md).

ink-gutter.$description: Dashboard theme only — absent in print/statement theme

column-label-width.$description: Wide multi-period table; up to 11 data columns

paper-legal.$description: Cross-cutting legal-document drafting-CONVENTION taxonomy (project-documents-20260717-consolidated-paper-legal-design-componen) — ONE shared base + 5 per-category variant deltas. This is a reusable CONVENTION register (heading form, numbering, cross-reference grammar), distinct from the concrete per-document-type components (legal-agency-suite, legal-prospectus, legal-subscription-agreement) that already ship real CSS. Most values below are PROVISIONAL placeholders — full CSS/pt values are being delivered incrementally by project-documents (Commercial first, from the Master JW9 pilot); do not treat as final until that lands. See paper-legal-conventions below for the qualitative per-variant rules (heading case, 'Section'/'Article' presence, cross-ref capitalization) that have no DTCG numeric/color equivalent.

legal-base.$description: Heading-agnostic shared formatting: Tinos type scale, hanging-ordinal clause ladder (.cl1/.cl2/.cl3), party/recital/signature/fee/schedule tables, draft stamp, page geometry. Only the font family is confirmed by the source request; exact pt sizes, line-heights, and margins are PROVISIONAL pending JW9 delivery.

commercial-agreement.$description: Flat 'N. Title.' bare-number, bold Title Case, terminal period, left-aligned, NOT all caps, NO 'ARTICLE'. Reference implementation: Master JW8/JW9 pilot (project-documents, not yet delivered as CSS here — Commercial variant CSS is the FIRST delivery expected).

constitutional-agreement.$description: Historical note: this vault's paper.semantic.legal-agreement.* tokens (accredited-investor fill-in booklets) collided with this same name until 2026-07-23, when they were renamed to paper.semantic.legal-subscription-agreement.* to close this collision (see that block's own $description). This description entry is left in place as a pointer for anyone who still remembers the old name.

schedule-exhibit.$description: 'SCHEDULE A' caps label, centered, page-break cover; internal headings inherit the parent variant's own scheme. Overlaps conceptually with the already-shipped legal-agency-suite component's own schedule-cover variant (apage...epage named counters, 7-variant MOU/Engagement-Letter family) — flagged for reconciliation with project-documents rather than built as a silent duplicate register.

letter.$description: Numbered paragraph, bold Title-Case run-in if headed, never all caps, usually no 'Section'/'Article' word. Overlaps conceptually with the already-shipped legal-agency-suite component's proposal-letter/mou-engagement-letter variants — flagged for reconciliation with project-documents rather than built as a silent duplicate register.

preliminary-instrument.$description: MOU numbered/lettered A./B.; LOI letter-form; term sheet table/bullets. No prior component coverage found in this vault — genuinely new ground, safe to build without a reconciliation question.

pdf-binder.$description: Interactive PDF-binder navigation system (slip-sheet TOC, HOME button). Point-space geometry from paper.primitive.pdf-nav.*, not a CSS @page box.

number-format.$description: Number-formatting conventions — string-valued, no DTCG numeric $type applies (these describe glyphs/rules, not measurements). Shared negative/tabular convention; nil glyph and page-number placement are deliberate per-family choices, not drift, and must not be collapsed to one value.

legal-subscription-agreement.negative: n/a — legal agreements do not carry tabular financial data
legal-subscription-agreement.page-number: single-letter schedules: "- " letter counter(letterpage) " -"; multi-character schedule IDs (e.g. B1/B2): "- " id "-" counter(idpage) " -" — see ordinal-marker/schedule-footer-format above, updated 2026-07-23

prospectus.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, single continuous counter (no per-schedule split)

agency-suite.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, per-schedule named counters A-E

financial-statement-yearend.currency-mark: single $ on the first data row only, no repeated $ per cell
financial-statement-yearend.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, Notes section only — adopted FROM the legal-agreement family's own convention

financial-report-layout.page-number: bottom-right, standard running counter — deliberately distinct from the yearend bundle's bottom-center Notes-only convention

paper-legal-conventions.$description: Per-category heading/numbering/cross-reference lock table for the paper-legal component family (source: project-documents-20260717-consolidated-paper-legal-design-componen §2). String-valued, no DTCG $type applies — these are drafting-convention rules, not measurements. Each cell marked HARD (never varies), DOMINANT (default; strong majority of filed-exhibit evidence), or HOUSE (accepted alternative, operator's call).

commercial-agreement.heading-form: Flat 'N. Title.' — bare number, bold Title Case, terminal period (DOMINANT). NOT all caps. Left-aligned (h2 delta; fixes the orphaned-clause-list defect a centered heading causes).
commercial-agreement.article-word: No — bare number (DOMINANT, Weagree: do not place 'Section' before the number). 'Section N.' = HOUSE alternative.
commercial-agreement.cross-ref-capitalization: Capital for internal refs ('Section 12', 'Section 12(h)'); lowercase for external refs ('section 13.7 of NI 31-103') (DOMINANT).

constitutional-agreement.heading-form: Article line 'ARTICLE N' + ALL-CAPS title, centered (DOMINANT); sub-level 'N.N Title' Title Case (DOMINANT). The two levels are always case-distinct (HARD).
constitutional-agreement.article-word: 'Article' = yes (DOMINANT). 'Section' at the N.N sub-level = HOUSE (Canadian practice: bare '1.1'; US practice: 'Section 1.01'). Include a convenience-construction clause (DOMINANT).

schedule-exhibit.heading-form: 'SCHEDULE A' caps label, centered; internal headings inherit the parent document's own scheme.
schedule-exhibit.article-word: The label itself IS the heading (yes). Pick one term — Schedule, Exhibit, or Annex — and hold it consistent throughout (HARD).
schedule-exhibit.cross-ref-capitalization: Capital, e.g. 'Schedule A' / 'Section 2.1 of Schedule A'.

letter.heading-form: Numbered paragraph; bold Title-Case run-in only if headed; never all caps.
letter.cross-ref-capitalization: Match the cross-reference word to whatever the divisions are actually called (HARD consistency rule): 'Section N' if headed, 'paragraph N' if bare.

preliminary-instrument.heading-form: MOU: numbered/lettered 'A./B.'; LOI: letter-form; term sheet: table/bullets.
preliminary-instrument.cross-ref-capitalization: Same match rule as letter; capital for internal refs.

drafting-rules-family-wide: No orphan subsection (near-hard): never a lone 'N.1' with no 'N.2' — a single-block section stays bare under its heading, with no decimal. [Weagree; Canada Justice Legistics; US House Manual on Drafting Style; Adams/MSCD]

Content-driven mixing is standard: subdivide only where 2+ co-ordinate provisions exist; uniform depth across a document is not required. [filed-exhibit: MDRNA/Canaccord 2009; Aptorum/H.C. Wainwright 2020; placement-agent EX-10.10 CIK 1047153]
Cross-reference address grammar has three depths that coexist: 'Section N' (whole) / 'Section N.N' (subsection) / 'Section N(x)' (lettered clause, cite THROUGH the section).

Internal vs external capitalization: capitalize refs to THIS agreement's own parts (Section/Article/Schedule); lowercase refs to statutes or other instruments (e.g. 'section 13.7 of NI 31-103' — statute title capitalized, pinpoint lowercase). Most commonly inconsistent rule in practice — enforce it.
External-reference disambiguation: always keep the 'of <instrument>' qualifier on an external reference so a same-numbered internal section is not misread.

Left-aligned heading is the orphaned-list fix mechanism: a centered heading empties the left margin, so a following indented clause list floats with nothing above it; left-aligning the heading is what the commercial-agreement h2 delta is doing, and it is intentional, not a stray override.
Roadmap chapeau is acceptable: an unnumbered lead-in paragraph under a subdivided section, cited as the whole section.

Do not formally define 'Section'/'Article' — capitalize without a definition; use a convenience-construction clause instead (e.g. 'references to a Section are to a section of this Agreement; headings for convenience only' — Mitel s.1.2; SEC LPA s.11.05 pattern).
The one HARD rule across the whole family: never two internal cross-reference pointers in different case within the same document.
market-practice-citations: [FILED-EXHIBIT] StandardAero UA (2026); CST Brands UA (2013) — flat '1. Title.' Title-Case sections.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Ares CRE UA; Baxter Intl UA — 'SECTION' label variants.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Smithfield/Shuanghui merger; Mitel Networks SHA (Ontario); SEC LPA CIK 1403528 — 'ARTICLE' caps + 'N.N'.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] MDRNA/Canaccord; Aptorum/H.C. Wainwright placement agreements — mixed subdivided/bare sections.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Libang Underwriting Agreement EX-1.1 (2024); Placement Agent Agreement EX-10.10 (CIK 1047153, 2009) — flat Section/N.N/(a), not ARTICLE.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Shareholders Agreement EX-10.19 (CIK 1500866); LP Agreement EX-10.21 (CIK 1403528) — ARTICLE + N.N.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Adams, A Manual of Style for Contract Drafting — all-caps readability defect; internal/external capitalization cue; enumeration requires 2+ units; article = a grouping choice.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Weagree — do not place 'Section' before the number; capitalize internal refs; articles advisable past ~7 sections or multiple topic groups.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Canada Justice Legistics; US House Manual on Drafting Style — at-least-two-parallel-units rule; statute references stay lowercase.
